title: Scripture for Life's Circumstances
source_boundary: These are Catholic study and prayer prompts, not medical, mental-health, legal, or emergency-care advice. Scripture passages are selected for pastoral reflection and are interpreted in conversation with the Catechism rather than as isolated promises.

source_documents.title: Catechism of the Catholic Church — official English edition
source_documents.authority: The Holy See / Libreria Editrice Vaticana
source_documents.use: Doctrinal context and official reading links

source_documents.title: Scripture Cards for Mental Health
source_documents.authority: United States Conference of Catholic Bishops
source_documents.use: Supplemental pastoral resource for entries explicitly marked with this source

source_documents.title: 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline — Get Help
source_documents.use: Crisis referral for the United States; not a Catholic doctrinal source

entries.title: Anxiety, fear, and peace
related_topics: Theological Virtues: Faith, Hope and Charity
entries.pastoral_note: Pray honestly and seek trusted pastoral and professional support when anxiety is persistent or overwhelming.

entries.title: Grief, death, and Christian hope
entries.pastoral_note: Christian hope does not deny grief. Bring loss to prayer and receive support from family, parish, and appropriate care.

entries.title: Illness, suffering, and endurance
related_topics: Redemptive Suffering and Carrying the Cross
entries.pastoral_note: Prayer accompanies medical care; it does not replace diagnosis, treatment, or emergency services.

entries.title: Forgiveness and reconciliation
entries.pastoral_note: Forgiveness does not require remaining in danger or avoiding necessary boundaries and justice.

entries.title: Prayer when it feels difficult
entries.pastoral_note: Difficulty in prayer can be part of the Christian journey; begin simply and remain connected to the Church's sacramental life.

entries.title: Discernment and seeking wisdom
entries.pastoral_note: Discernment is formed by prayer, conscience, sound counsel, and the teaching life of the Church.

entries.title: Loneliness and belonging
related_topics: The Church as the Body of Christ
entries.pastoral_note: The Church is a communion; consider speaking with a parish, trusted friend, or pastoral minister rather than carrying isolation alone.

entries.title: Family conflict and charity
related_topics: Theological Virtues: Faith, Hope and Charity
entries.pastoral_note: Charity includes truth, safety, and appropriate boundaries. Seek qualified help when conflict involves abuse or danger.

entries.title: Temptation and perseverance
related_topics: The Ten Commandments in the New Covenant
entries.pastoral_note: Christian perseverance normally includes practical safeguards, sacramental confession, accountability, and prayer.

entries.title: Despair, crisis, or thoughts of self-harm
related_topics: Theological Virtues: Faith, Hope and Charity
entries.pastoral_note: If there is immediate danger or thoughts of self-harm, seek emergency help now. In the United States, call or text 988; elsewhere, contact local emergency services or a crisis line. Scripture and prayer are not substitutes for urgent care.

entries.title: Work, provision, and financial pressure
related_topics: Theological Virtues: Faith, Hope and Charity
entries.pastoral_note: Bring financial pressure to prayer while taking responsible practical steps, seeking qualified advice where needed, and avoiding promises of quick religious solutions.

entries.title: Guilt, mercy, and returning to God
entries.pastoral_note: Christian repentance receives God's mercy and also takes responsibility for repair, justice, and appropriate accountability.

entries.title: Vocation, service, and following Christ
entries.pastoral_note: A vocation is discerned patiently through prayer, the sacraments, concrete service, wise counsel, and the needs God places before us.

entries.title: Anger, peacemaking, and self-control
related_topics: Theological Virtues: Faith, Hope and Charity
entries.pastoral_note: Anger can signal a real wound or injustice; respond without violence, protect safety, and seek reconciliation where it is possible and prudent.
